e-6570.problem: Given that $D=\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}}{\textrm d x^{2}}+3 \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}+5,$ what is $D(y)$ for $y=e^{- x}?$
e-6570.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = a_{2}\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + a_{1}\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + a_0y
$$

with constant coefficients  $a_2 = 1, a_1 = 3,$ and $a_0 = 5.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-x}) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+5){e}^{-x} \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-x})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})+5{e}^{-x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{e}^{-x})+3\cdot (-{e}^{-x})+5{e}^{-x} \\  & ={e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+5{e}^{-x} \\  & =3{e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
$$

e-6571.knowledge_point: Applying Differential Operators With Functions of X as Coefficients
e-6571.problem: Given that $D=x^2\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}}{\textrm d x^{3}}-5x \dfrac{\textrm d^{2}}{\textrm d x^{2}} +9\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x},$ what is $D(y)$ for $y=\ln{x}?$
e-6571.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = f_{3}(x)\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} + f_{2}(x)\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + f_{1}(x)\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + f_0(x)y.
$$

with $f_3 = x^2, f_2 = -5x, f_1 = 9,$ and $f_0 = 0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-5x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-5x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{x})-5x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})+9\cdot (\frac{1}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-5x(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+\frac{9}{x} \\  & ={x}^{2}(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})+\frac{5}{x}+\frac{9}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{x}+\frac{5}{x}+\frac{9}{x} \\  & =\frac{16}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

e-21785.knowledge_point: Applying Differential Operators With Multivariable Functions as Coefficients
e-21785.problem: If $D(y)=y\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} - \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} + y^3,$ then calculate $D(e^{3x}).$
e-21785.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = f_{3}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} +  f_{2}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + f_{1}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + f_0(x,y)y
$$

with $f_3 = y,  f_2 = 0,  f_1 = -1,$ and $f_0 = y^2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y = e^{3x}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{x}) & ={e}^{3x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{3x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{3x})+{({e}^{3x})}^{3} \\  & ={e}^{3x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(3{e}^{3x})-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & ={e}^{3x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{3x})-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & =27{e}^{6x}-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & ={e}^{3x}({e}^{6x}+27{e}^{3x}-3)\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=5,$ and ${a}_{0}=1.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))+1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))+5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Given that D=d2dx2−2ddx, what is D(y) for y=cos⁡x?

a
2sin⁡x−cos⁡x
b
3sin⁡x
c
2cos⁡x+sin⁡x
d
−3cos⁡x
e
−sin⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: For y=cos(x), y'=-sin(x) and y''=-cos(x). Thus D(y)=y''-2y'=-cos(x)+2sin(x), which is option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=-2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-2(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

D(y)=a2d2ydx2+a1dydx+a0y with constant coefficients a2=1,a1=−2, and a0=0.

D(y)=D(cos⁡x)=(d2dx2−2ddx)(cos⁡x)=d2dx2(cos⁡x)−2ddx(cos⁡x)=ddx(−sin⁡x)−2(−sin⁡x)=−cos⁡x+2sin⁡x=2sin⁡x−cos⁡x

$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=-2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$

decision.explanation: For y=sin²(x), y'=sin(2x), y''=2cos(2x), and y'''=-4sin(2x). Therefore D(y)=y'''+2y'=-2sin(2x), matching option d.

after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}){sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({sin}^{2}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({sin}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\end{aligned}
$$

Given that D=d3dx3+2ddx, what is D(y) for y=sin2⁡x?

a
0
b
2sin⁡2x+cos⁡2x
c
4sin⁡2x
d
−2sin⁡2x
e
4sin⁡2x−2cos⁡2x

Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=a3d3ydx3+a2d2ydx2+a1dydx+a0y with constant coefficients a3=1,a2=0,a1=2, and a0=0.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(cos⁡2x)=(d3dx3+2ddx)sin2⁡x=d3dx3(sin2⁡x)+2ddx(sin2⁡x)=d2dx2(sin⁡2x)+2⋅(sin⁡2x)=ddx(2cos⁡2x)+2sin⁡2x=−4sin⁡2x+2sin⁡2x=−2sin⁡2x

$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}){sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({sin}^{2}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({sin}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\end{aligned}

before.html:
Question 4
?

Given that D=d2dx2+2ddx−5, what is D(y) for y=sin⁡(3x)?

a
−14sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
b
−9sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
c
−14sin⁡(3x)−6cos⁡(3x)
d
14sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
e
6cos⁡(3x)
Submit

decision.explanation: For y=sin(3x), y'=3cos(3x) and y''=-9sin(3x). Thus D(y)=y''+2y'-5y=-14sin(3x)+6cos(3x), matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=-5.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-5)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+2\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Given that D=d2dx2+2ddx−5, what is D(y) for y=sin⁡(3x)?

a
−14sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
b
−9sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
c
−14sin⁡(3x)−6cos⁡(3x)
d
14sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)
e
6cos⁡(3x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=a2d2ydx2+a1dydx+a0y with constant coefficients a2=1,a1=2, and a0=−5.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(sin⁡(3x))=(d2dx2+2ddx−5)sin⁡(3x)=d2dx2(sin⁡(3x))+2ddx(sin⁡(3x))−5⋅sin⁡(3x)=ddx(3cos⁡(3x))+2⋅(3cos⁡(3x))−5sin⁡(3x)=−9sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)−5sin⁡(3x)=−14sin⁡(3x)+6cos⁡(3x)

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms y'=3cos(3x) and y''=-9sin(3x). Therefore D(y)=y''+2y'-5y=-14sin(3x)+6cos(3x), which is option a.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Differential Operators With Constant Coefficients
content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=-5.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-5)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+2\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The constant 2 has zero derivatives. Since y'=-e^{-x} and y'''=-e^{-x}, D(y)=2y'''-3y'=-2e^{-x}+3e^{-x}=e^{-x}, matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=2,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=-3,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =(2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{-x}+2)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(-{e}^{-x})-3\cdot (-{e}^{-x}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})+3{e}^{-x} \\  & =-2{e}^{-x}+3{e}^{-x} \\  & ={e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Given that D=2d3dx3−3ddx, what is D(y) for y=e−x+2?

a
2
b
e−x
c
−5e−x
d
5e−x
e
−3e−x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=a3d3ydx3+a2d2ydx2+a1dydx+a0y with constant coefficients a3=2,a2=0,a1=−3, and a0=0.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(e−x+2)=(2d3dx3−3ddx)(e−x+2)=2d3dx3(e−x+2)−3ddx(e−x+2)=2d2dx2(−e−x)−3⋅(−e−x)=2ddx(e−x)+3e−x=−2e−x+3e−x=e−x

content.knowledge_point: Applying Differential Operators With Constant Coefficients
content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=2,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=-3,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =(2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{-x}+2)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(-{e}^{-x})-3\cdot (-{e}^{-x}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})+3{e}^{-x} \\  & =-2{e}^{-x}+3{e}^{-x} \\  & ={e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Given that D=xd2dx2+2xddx−3, what is D(y) for y=1x?

a
2x2+5x
b
2x2−5x
c
−5x
d
2x2
e
−2x2−5x
Submit

decision.explanation: For y=1/x, y'=-1/x² and y''=2/x³. Thus D(y)=xy''+2xy'-3y=2/x²-2/x-3/x=2/x²-5/x, matching option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=2x,$ and ${f}_{0}=-3.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-3)\frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{x})+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})-3\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+2x(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =x\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{2}{x}-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5}{x}\end{aligned}

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x)d2ydx2+f1(x)dydx+f0(x)y with f2=x,f1=2x, and f0=−3.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y: D(y)=D(1x)=(xd2dx2+2xddx−3)1x=xd2dx2(1x)+2xddx(1x)−3⋅1x=xddx(−1x2)+2x(−1x2)−3x=x⋅2x3−2x−3x=2x2−5x

content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=2x,$ and ${f}_{0}=-3.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-3)\frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{x})+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})-3\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+2x(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =x\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{2}{x}-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=2,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y.
$$

with ${f}_{3}={x}^{2},{f}_{2}=-2x,{f}_{1}=x,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{4}) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}){x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({x}^{4})-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{4})+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(4{x}^{3})-2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{3})+x(4{x}^{3}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2})-2x(12{x}^{2})+4{x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}(24x)-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =24{x}^{3}-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =4{x}^{4}\end{aligned}

Given that D=x2d3dx3−2xd2dx2+xddx, what is D(y) for y=x4?

a
 48x3
b
 4x4+16x3
c
 16x3
d
 4x4
e
 4x3−24x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form D(y)=f3(x)d3ydx3+f2(x)d2ydx2+f1(x)dydx+f0(x)y. with f3=x2,f2=−2x,f1=x, and f0=0.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(x4)=(x2d3dx3−2xd2dx2+xddx)x4=x2d3dx3(x4)−2xd2dx2(x4)+xddx(x4)=x2d2dx2(4x3)−2xddx(4x3)+x(4x3)=x2ddx(12x2)−2x(12x2)+4x4=x2(24x)−24x3+4x4=24x3−24x3+4x4=4x4

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms y'=4x³, y''=12x², and y'''=24x. Hence D(y)=x²(24x)-2x(12x²)+x(4x³)=4x⁴, so option d is correct.

content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y.
$$

with ${f}_{3}={x}^{2},{f}_{2}=-2x,{f}_{1}=x,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{4}) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}){x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({x}^{4})-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{4})+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(4{x}^{3})-2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{3})+x(4{x}^{3}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2})-2x(12{x}^{2})+4{x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}(24x)-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =24{x}^{3}-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =4{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: For y=x²-1, y'=2x and y''=2. Thus D(y)=x²y''+3y'+2y=2x²+6x+2(x²-1)=4x²+6x-2, matching option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}={x}^{2},{f}_{1}=3,$ and ${f}_{0}=2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{2}-1) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+2)({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-1)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)+3(2x)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 2+6x+2{x}^{2}-2 \\  & =4{x}^{2}+6x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Given that D=x2d2dx2+3ddx+2, what is D(y) for y=x2−1?

a
2x2+6x−2
b
6x−2
c
4x2+6x+2
d
4x2−6x−2
e
4x2+6x−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x)d2ydx2+f1(x)dydx+f0(x)y with f2=x2,f1=3, and f0=2.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y: D(y)=D(x2−1)=(x2d2dx2+3ddx+2)(x2−1)=x2d2dx2(x2−1)+3ddx(x2−1)+2(x2−1)=x2ddx(2x)+3(2x)+2(x2−1)=x2⋅2+6x+2x2−2=4x2+6x−2

content.knowledge_point: Applying Differential Operators With Functions of X as Coefficients
content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}={x}^{2},{f}_{1}=3,$ and ${f}_{0}=2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{2}-1) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+2)({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-1)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)+3(2x)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 2+6x+2{x}^{2}-2 \\  & =4{x}^{2}+6x-2\end{aligned}
$$

If D(y)=yd2ydx2−xydydx+5y, then D(x2+1)=

a
(x2+1)(7−x2)
b
(x2+1)(7+2x2)
c
(x2+1)(7−2x2)
d
(x2+1)(5−2x2)
e
(x2+1)(2x2−7)
Submit

If D(y)=yd2ydx2−xydydx+5y, then D(x2+1)=

a
(x2+1)(7−x2)
b
(x2+1)(7+2x2)
c
(x2+1)(7−2x2)
d
(x2+1)(5−2x2)
e
(x2+1)(2x2−7)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x,y)d2ydx2+f1(x,y)dydx+f0(x,y)y with f2=y,f1=−xy, and f0=5.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y=x2+1: D(x2+1)=(x2+1)d2dx2(x2+1)−x(x2+1)ddx(x2+1)+5(x2+1)=(x2+1)ddx(2x)−x(x2+1)⋅2x+5(x2+1)=(x2+1)⋅2−2x2(x2+1)+5(x2+1)=2(x2+1)−2x2(x2+1)+5(x2+1)=7(x2+1)−2x2(x2+1)=(x2+1)(7−2x2)

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that y'=2x and y''=2. Substitution gives D(y)=2(x²+1)-2x²(x²+1)+5(x²+1)=(x²+1)(7-2x²), matching option c.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=2y,$ and ${f}_{0}=3y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={e}^{-2x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{-2x}) & ={e}^{-2x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-2x})+2({e}^{-2x})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-2x})+3{({e}^{-2x})}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{-2x})+2{e}^{-2x}\cdot (-2{e}^{-2x})+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\cdot 4{e}^{-2x}-4{e}^{-4x}+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & =4{e}^{-4x}-4{e}^{-4x}+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & =3{e}^{-4x}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: For y=cos(2x), y''=-4cos(2x)=-4y. Therefore D(y)=yy''+4y²=-4y²+4y²=0, matching option a.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=0,$ and ${f}_{0}=4y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+4{(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+4{cos}^{2}⁡2x \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+4{cos}^{2}⁡2x \\  & =-4{cos}^{2}⁡2x+4{cos}^{2}⁡2x \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x,y)d2ydx2+f1(x,y)dydx+f0(x,y)y with f2=y,f1=0, and f0=4y.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y=cos⁡2x: D(cos⁡2x)=cos⁡2xd2dx2(cos⁡2x)+4(cos⁡2x)2=cos⁡2xddx(−2sin⁡2x)+4cos2⁡2x=cos⁡2x(−4cos⁡2x)+4cos2⁡2x=−4cos2⁡2x+4cos2⁡2x=0

a
2(−5−2x3+3x6)
b

decision.explanation: For y=x³+1, y'=3x² and y'''=6. Thus D(y)=(x³+1)(6-6x³+4)=10+4x³-6x⁶=2(5+2x³-3x⁶), matching option b.

Question 15

If D(y)=yd3ydx3−2xydydx+4y, then D(x3+1)=

a
2(−5−2x3+3x6)
b
2(5+2x3−3x6)
c
2(5+2x3+3x6)
d
2(5+4x3−3x6)
e
2(5−2x3−3x6)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f3(x,y)d3ydx3+f1(x,y)dydx+f0(x,y)y with f3=y,f1=−2xy, and f0=4.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y=x3+1: D(x3+1)=(x3+1)d3dx3(x3+1)−2x(x3+1)ddx(x3+1)+4(x3+1)=(x3+1)d2dx2(3x2)−2x(x3+1)⋅3x2+4(x3+1)=(x3+1)ddx(6x)−6x3(x3+1)+4(x3+1)=(x3+1)⋅6−6x3(x3+1)+4(x3+1)=6(x3+1)−6x3(x3+1)+4(x3+1)=10+4x3−6x6=2(5+2x3−3x6)
